s1.syndrome_frame: Acute to subacute onset of headache and vision loss with sinus inflammation and orbital involvement
salient_findings: Severe headache with worsening over time
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation and bony erosion
Extension of inflammation into the orbital apex
key_facts: Patient is a man in his 70s
No history of chronic or allergic rhinosinusitis
Recent diagnosis of COVID-19 with recovery
Developed rhinorrhea three weeks prior to presentation
Worsening right-sided headache over time
Right eye visual acuity limited to hand-motion detection
Severe pain on ocular motion
Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation on imaging
Bony erosion of the medial orbital apex bone with extension of inflammation
Positive sinus cultures for Streptococcus constellatus
Elevated Serum IgG4 levels
Dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells on pathology

differentials: Rosai-Dorfman disease variant with IgG4-positive plasma cells
Chronic lymphocytic inflammation with pontine expansion
per_call: Rosai-Dorfman disease variant with IgG4-positive plasma cells
Chronic lymphocytic inflammation with pontine expansion

shortlist.label: IgG4-related disease
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated Serum IgG4 levels and dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells on pathology

shortlist.label: Invasive bacterial rhinosinusitis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive sinus cultures for Streptococcus constellatus and symptoms of worsening headache and vision loss

shortlist.label: Orbital cellulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Severe pain on ocular motion and opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation on imaging

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Inflammation of the sinuses and orbital involvement, although less likely given the absence of other systemic symptoms

shortlist.label: Allergic fungal sinusitis
shortlist.why_kept: Opacification of all sinuses on the right with diffuse inflammation on imaging, although less likely given the absence of other allergic symptoms

raw.rationale: Elevated Serum IgG4 levels and dense infiltrate of IgG-containing plasma cells on pathology, consistent with IgG4-related disease, along with clinical presentation of worsening headache and vision loss

rejected.label: Invasive bacterial rhinosinusitis
rejected.why: Although positive sinus cultures for Streptococcus constellatus, the presence of elevated IgG4 levels and characteristic pathology findings point more towards IgG4-related disease

rejected.label: Orbital cellulitis
rejected.why: Lack of specific findings indicative of orbital cellulitis, such as significant proptosis or eyelid swelling, and presence of systemic and pathological indicators of IgG4-related disease

rejected.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rejected.why: No mention of systemic vasculitis or other organ involvement typical of granulomatosis with polyangiitis, and specific indicators of IgG4-related disease are present

rejected.label: Allergic fungal sinusitis
rejected.why: No evidence of fungal elements or allergic mucin, and the presence of elevated IgG4 levels and characteristic IgG4-positive plasma cell infiltrate
